WHAT YOU’RE SEEING

A LITTLE EXPERIMENT

Watch the Sun orbit too.

Start a five-solar-mass black hole eight AU from the Sun with sideways velocity. Both move around their shared center of mass. Watch which planets remain bound.

Inside this model +

This is a two-dimensional Newtonian N-body model. All eight planets and up to two stellar-mass objects exert gravity on each other. Initial orbits are circular and coplanar; positions are illustrative, not today’s sky.

Distance is in astronomical units (AU), mass in solar masses (M☉), and time in years. Velocity Verlet integration limits each step by both the gravitational timescale and the relative crossing speed, so fast encounters are not skipped. At 1×, one real second advances about 0.03 simulated years, with automatic slowing during difficult encounters. The default camera follows the system center of mass; it does not pin the Sun in place. Drag to pan, zoom with the wheel or buttons, and use Fit all to recover bodies outside the view. The Milky Way option is a separate static distance map: it does not add galactic gravity to this local experiment. Its disk size and the Sun’s location are approximate; the outer galaxy and halo are not bounded by the drawn disk. NASA: galactic distances ↗

Changing the central mass or adding an object is an instantaneous thought experiment. Choose a tangential two-body circular speed √(G(M₁+M₂)/r), zero relative velocity for direct infall, or 1.5 times circular speed for a flyby. Other planets perturb these ideal initial conditions; an orbit is not guaranteed. The full system is shifted into its center-of-mass rest frame on insertion. A one-solar-mass black hole is a hypothetical comparison, not a normal stellar remnant.

Ordinary bodies combine on physical contact using estimated radii. Black-hole encounters combine at the larger of contact radius, an approximate tidal radius R(MBH/m)^(1/3), or a 0.0001 AU resolution floor. The result is a point mass representing the black hole plus unresolved material, not instantaneous physical accretion. Mass and linear momentum are conserved; unresolved angular momentum is stored as spin. Mechanical energy is not conserved by this inelastic prescription. Escaping gas, radiation, debris dynamics, and relativity are omitted. Surviving bodies continue to evolve. Body sizes are enlarged; the rings around a black hole are schematic. Faint circular guides mark initial planetary distances and disappear after you alter the system; trails show the calculated paths.

Gravity: a = GM/r². Circular speed: v = √(GM/r). Background: NASA’s black hole guide ↗
